text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"“I also do question the safety it has” followed by reasons about testing and moral choices","quality":"argument development","description":"It develops a clearer line of reasoning by giving multiple supporting points for its position instead of mainly restating approval."},{"evidence":"“fully one-hundred percent driverless” and “A computer wont figure out those kinds of morals”","quality":"specific counterargument","description":"It engages a more substantive concern about safety and moral decision-making, which strengthens the argumentative depth."},{"evidence":"“we still should pay attention and take precautions” and “I don't believe these vehicles can make moral choices”","quality":"qualification","description":"It presents a more nuanced stance by supporting driverless cars while setting limits on how far automation should go."},{"evidence":"“But I wouldn't buy one anytime soon” and “When the day comes and they are safer”","quality":"conditional reasoning","description":"It shows better reasoning about real-world adoption by tying support to improved safety rather than making an unconditional claim."}]}
